MARKET.head: Calabria Family's Bélena launches 200ml minis across Pinot Grigio, Moscato and Rosé
MARKET.summ: As Australian wine preferences shift and drinking occasions continue to evolve, the Calabria Family is looking beyond the traditional 750ml bottle with its new 200ml Bélena minis. The new format is across the brand’s most popular styles, including Pinot Grigio, Moscato and Rosé. It will arrive in stores from January 2027 and...
takeaways: Calabria Family is launching 200ml Bélena minis in Pinot Grigio, Moscato and Rosé from January 2027.
The minis will be distributed nationally in Australia by the House of Fine Wine network.
Bélena reports domestic sales growth of 20% despite an overall decline in the Australian wine category.

MARKET.head: VinePair's weekly roundup covers spending, Chianti rosé, and industry product releases
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. This week, we have updates on household spending on alcohol in the U.S., the EU’s approval of Chianti rosé, the latest product releases, and more.
takeaways: It cites U.S. household alcohol spending, an EU approval of Chianti rosé, and recent product releases, without details or figures.
Other roundup editions in the material mention Heineken, RNDC, Diageo, and Uncle Nearest, but their specifics are not reported in this text.

MARKET.head: Moldova pitches indigenous grapes and 23 producers at ProWine Shanghai
MARKET.summ: With 23 wine and spirits producers heading to ProWine Shanghai, the export-driven country is putting indigenous grapes and competitive pricing at the center of its pitch
takeaways: Twenty-three Moldovan wine and spirits producers will seek business with Chinese importers at ProWine Shanghai, November 10 to 12.
Chinese customs data show Moldovan wine imports reached US$1.43 million in the first nine months of 2026.
About 85% of Moldovan production is exported, and the EU now takes roughly 60% of its wine exports.

MARKET.head: Australian wine's small formats gain ground as moderation and single-person households grow
MARKET.summ: Consumer demand for wine is changing globally, and while this has shown up in many mature markets as a decline in consumption, the shift in consumption habits has also uncovered an increasing consumer interest in smaller, more flexible packaging formats.
takeaways: Combined export and domestic off-trade sales of 187mL wine packs rose 22 per cent to almost 1.9 million litres in 2025-26.
Export volumes of 187mL packs grew 39 per cent from 2023-24 to 2025-26, concentrated in Asia-Pacific markets.
Single-person households make up 26 per cent of Australian households, up from 18 per cent in 1981, per Census data.

MARKET.head: EU greenwashing directive takes effect, restricting vague eco claims on wine
MARKET.summ: New restrictions on environmental marketing claims are putting terms like “natural” and “eco-friendly” under the microscope, prompting questions about what wineries can and can’t include on bottle labels
takeaways: Directive (EU) 2024/825, also called EmpCo, bans vague environmental claims like "eco-friendly" and "green" from wine marketing and labels.
Enforcement began September 27, with fines up to four percent of annual turnover, applied by individual EU member states.
Old stock is not grandfathered in, so producers are using stickers or point-of-sale information to correct existing claims.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux takes 41% of traded wine value as Burgundy's share jumps
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux strengthened its lead of the market, claiming 41% of traded value. Burgundy’s share also rose compared to last week
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded value on the Liv-ex wine market, extending its lead.
Burgundy's share of traded value rose from 15.7% last week to 20.8% this week.
Champagne's share fell from 13.0% to 8.5%, while Tuscany claimed 11.6% of traded value.

MARKET.head: India's EU trade deal to cut wine tariffs, but state rules complicate entry
MARKET.summ: For years, India has occupied a peculiar position in the international wine industry: too large to ignore, too complicated to enter
takeaways: The India-EU Free Trade Agreement will cut India's 150% tariff on EU wine to 20% for premium and 30% for medium wines, phased in.
Alcohol is regulated state by state in India, so exporters must plan market entry for each state rather than nationally.
India imported 5.4 million litres of wine worth US$28.8 million in 2025, up 13.7% in volume and 10.9% in value.

MARKET.head: German wine imports into China rise in volume, value and price this year
MARKET.summ: Imports rose in volume, value and average price in the first nine months, offering an encouraging backdrop for 45 wineries and importers heading to the German Pavilion
takeaways: China imported 4.23 million litres of bottled German wine in the first nine months of 2026, up 8%.
Import value rose 11% to US$22.49 million, while the average import price increased 3%.
Germany brings 45 wineries and importers to ProWine Shanghai, Nov. 10-12, including over 10 first-time Chinese exhibitors.

CULTURE.head: Beaujolais Nouveau's midnight release became wine's first viral, hype-driven launch
CULTURE.summ: Decades before brands built anticipation for limited-edition drops with countdowns, celebrity appearances, or social media buzz, wine had its own version of the hype cycle. The days may be shorter and the air crisper, but in the world of wine, November is when things start heating up. This is especially true for those who have...
takeaways: Beaujolais Nouveau, made from Gamay in France, is released at 12:01 a.m. on the third Thursday of November, a date set in 1985 by INAO.
Négociant Georges Duboeuf, founder of his house in 1964, helped turn the release into an international event with stunts like a 1988 horseback truck departure.
Carbonic maceration lets the wine go from vine to bottle in six to eight weeks, producing a light, fruity style meant for drinking soon after release.

CULTURE.head: Charlotte Newton named Dux of 2026 Len Evans Tutorial in Hunter Valley
CULTURE.summ: Charlotte Newton, owner and winemaker at Cha Cha Wines in Western Australia, has been awarded the Basil Sellers Prize for Dux of the 2026 Len Evans Tutorial. Newton, along with 11 other Australian wine professionals, took part in the 24th Tutorial held at Spicer’s Guesthouse in the Hunter Valley from 2 to 6 November.
takeaways: Charlotte Newton, owner and winemaker at Cha Cha Wines in Western Australia, was named Dux of the 2026 Len Evans Tutorial.
Twelve scholars, picked from a record 193 applications, took part in the tutorial at Spicer's Guesthouse in the Hunter Valley from 2 to 6 November.
As Dux, Newton receives $10,000 to further her global wine education.

CULTURE.head: Orlando Cellar 13 Grenache takes top prize at James Halliday Grenache Challenge
CULTURE.summ: The Orlando 2025 Cellar 13 Grenache has received the highest accolade at the 10th annual James Halliday Grenache Challenge, judged in McLaren Vale on 20th October 2026. The judges assessed 169 single-varietal Grenache wines from around Australia, “celebrating the growing strength and incredible diversity of the variety”.
takeaways: At the 10th James Halliday Grenache Challenge in McLaren Vale, judges named Orlando's 2025 Cellar 13 Grenache the top wine from 169 entries.
Chief judge Tony Barlow called it a worthy winner, with the final tasting margin between six Grenaches from three regions very close.
The competition's judges also named Big Easy Radio 2025 Perpetual Holidaze Grenache and S.C. Pannell 2024 Little Branch Grenache as top wines.

CULTURE.head: Dan Sims named chair of Melbourne Royal Wine Awards Committee
CULTURE.summ: Melbourne Royal has appointed respected wine industry figure Dan Sims, chair of Wine Victoria, as chair of the Melbourne Royal Wine Awards Committee, bringing “extensive industry experience, leadership and a deep commitment to the continued success of one of Australia’s most prestigious wine competitions”.
takeaways: The committee is made up of representatives from across the Australian wine industry and oversees the competition's program.
Sims will co-present this year's awards with Kirrily Waldhorn, Melbourne Royal senior manager food & beverage awards, at the Trophy Awards Presentation.

CULTURE.head: Alison Smith Story of Smith Story Wines describes her path into the wine business
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Alison Smith Story, of Smith Story Wine Cellars, is the guest on VinePair's Wine 101 podcast hosted by Keith Beavers.
The episode is a casual conversation about how Story fell into the wine business and her journey in wine.
The podcast is sponsored by Wines of Alsace and the Alsace Rocks campaign.

SCIENCE.head: AWRI updates agrochemical and MRL search app on Apple and Google stores
SCIENCE.summ: 9 November 2026 The Australian Wine Research Institute has updated the version of the AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on both the Apple App … more
takeaways: The Australian Wine Research Institute has released an updated version of its AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on Apple and Google Play.
The free app gives rapid access to information in the 'Agrochemicals registered for use in Australian viticulture' booklet, known as the 'Dog book'.
Users who already have the app are asked to install the update so they keep receiving future updates.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Tasting some Ports from Quinta do Infantado, an important Douro producer
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Infantado is a family-owned Quinta dating back to 1816. They were famous for being the first quinta to
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Quinta do Infantado, a family-owned Douro estate dating to 1816, was first to bottle Port in the Douro in 1979 rather than in Vila Nova de Gaia.
João Roseira heads the 46-hectare Covas de Douro estate, with cousin Álvaro Roseira in charge of winemaking; Graft is the new UK importer for its Ports.
Tasting notes rate the Ports 93 to 95 out of 100, including a 2015 Vintage Port scored 95 and a 2021 Late Bottled Vintage at 50 g/l sugar.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Vinography Images: Slice of Italy
NEWSLETTERS.summ: What else do you need really? A little farmhouse, a patch of grapes, some olive trees, and the rolling hills
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow
takeaways: Vinography's image post shows an Italian farmhouse set among grapevines, olive trees and rolling hills.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Bourgueil’s Aurélien Revillot
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Through a Burgundian lens, Cabernet Franc becomes a study of place and terroir, parcel by parcel
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Aurélien Revillot is a relative newcomer to Bourgueil, and his domaine is part of Becky Wasserman's portfolio.
Revillot has three finished cuvées, with two additional cuvées parcellaires set to join from the 2020 vintage.
Revillot, from a Mâconnais farming family, trained in Dijon and worked at Domaine Drouhin in Oregon and Newton Johnson in South Africa.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Catalonia’s Under(wine)world
NEWSLETTERS.summ: How a Champagne trip in the 1800s resulted in a new Spanish wine in a league of its own
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Josep Raventós of Penedès produced Spain's first traditional method sparkling wine in 1872, with second fermentation in the bottle, using Spanish indigenous grapes.
Cava takes its name from the cellars, or caves, dug in Sant Sadurní d'Anoia, which can reach 20 m deep, and became the formal label term under Spanish law in 1972.
Finca Sumarroca's 2022 Gran Reserva Brut Nature Cava, made from Macabeu, Xarel•lo and Parellada, aged 40 months and sells for $28 Cdn.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing and was set to visit Guangzhou on November 6.
Spain ranked fifth by volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but only a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
The author highlighted Piqueras' El Abuelo, a blend of Alicante Bouschet, Monastrell and Syrah, as standout value among roadshow wines.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Why I Enjoy Wine Competition Judging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Plus a guide to Le Puy wines - my notes from a recent vertical tasting
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Le Puy, a right-bank Bordeaux estate of 54 hectares farmed biodynamically, left the Francs Côtes de Bordeaux appellation in 2017 and now bottles as Vin de France.
Le Puy's entry cuvée Emilien costs €30, €40 in Europe, $50 in the US, or £60 in the UK, with the grand vin Barthélemy around triple those prices.
At the Asia Wine Trophy in Daejeon, a Georgian Khikhvi amber earned an instant grand gold, with all six judges scoring it in the mid-90s.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Traditional labels? Suck My Duck
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Never say that wine labelling regulations are a subject devoid of humour. The Tribunal Correctionnel de Paris recently heard a case brought by anti-alcohol NGO Addictions France against Languedoc vigneron Nicolas Vellas over his provocative packaging. Vellas’s edgy cuvées have included “Little Fuck,” “Bad Angel” (its label...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: A Paris court heard a case by anti-alcohol group Addictions France against Languedoc vigneron Nicolas Vellas over provocative labels like "Suck My Duck".
The case tests whether such packaging breaches France's 1991 Loi Évin, which restricts alcohol advertising, and the court reportedly held it adjourned for now.
Bordeaux has lost a fifth of its vineyard area in four years, with 30,000 ha uprooted by end-December, while its labels remain conservative.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The 2026 Harvest Is In , Here’s What It’s Already Telling Us About this Burgundy Wine Vintage
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Early harvest data from the 2026 Burgundy vintage reveals exciting insights into the region's grapes, offering a first look at vine yields and pricing
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Burgundy's Côte d'Or picking finished between 10 and 12 September, and the Comité des Vins de Bourgogne called the 2026 harvest the earliest ever recorded.
Early estimates passed on by the Comité suggest Burgundy's 2026 crop is down around 30 per cent against the five-year average.
Agreste forecasts Pinot Noir losses in Burgundy of more than half, while Champagne's harvest is seen down by almost half.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Essential Kit for Kitchen Season
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Outfitting your kitchen with the season’s essential tools, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker says the clocks dropping back on Sunday, Oct 30, 2026, marks the start of what she calls Kitchen Season.
Maker says November and December bring a special urge to cook for others and to revive family recipes or try new cuisines.
Maker's article lists kitchen tools she uses year-round that become even more essential during festive cooking, with no affiliate links.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A deeper look at underwater wine aging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Is a wine from the depths ‘better’ or does it depend on the boat?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Attis, a winery owned by the Fariña family in O Grove near Pontevedra, Galicia, aged magnum bottles of its Albariño under the estuary's waters.
The underwater-aged wine is the 2025 Attis Albariño 'Mar', aged five months at 13-16C and sealed with glass caps instead of cork.
The author's past tastings of underwater-aged wines suggested gimmickry, finding them more advanced in age than landbound counterparts.
